solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very large area in which son's buried bones

definitions.note: plural noun, as the Latin plural is

indicators.note: the son is buried, so his letter is sunk inside the other pieces

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's is just 'is'

explanation.surface: A vast plot of land in which a son has been laid to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: OSSA is the Latin plural of os, a bone, familiar from anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the anatomical Latin word for the skeleton's individual pieces.

clue.text: With charm, agent probes Constable collections on his own

indicators.note: the agent probes, pushing into the middle of the collections

parts.note: a posse is a band gathered by a sheriff or constable, so posses are his collections
a rep (representative) is a sales agent
singly means one at a time, alone

explanation.surface: A dealer delves into the painter John Constable's art collections without help.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable looks like the painter, but it is a lawman whose collections are posses.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in an attractive, appealing manner is done winningly, with charm.

clue.text: Half-rampant nude for the most part covering lower half — this?

definitions.text: Half-rampant nude for the most part covering lower half — this?

parts.note: the top half of the word nude, its first two letters, rears up (rampant) and so reads upwards in this down entry

indicators.note: the word for most part goes round the bottom piece, covering it

parts.note: mainly means for the most part
the lower half of the word nude in a down entry is its last two letters

explanation.surface: A partly rearing naked figure, mostly covering the lower body: is this how a modest girl behaves?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the top of a word is its start, so 'rampant' (rearing up) flips the top half of nude, and its lower half is what gets covered. The whole clue also describes the immodest pose.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodest, unbecoming behaviour of the kind a young girl was once expected to avoid.

clue.text: Comedy Theatre perhaps impressed by science fiction author's novel

indicators.note: the theatre is pressed into the abbreviation, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a comedy venue might fancifully be called a house of laughter
the author is the setter, I, and author's is 'I have', I'VE

explanation.surface: A London theatre staging comedy has caught the eye of a sci-fi writer's book.
explanation.walkthrough: The Comedy Theatre is a real West End theatre in London; here it is just an example of a laughter house. The novel is Kurt Vonnegut's anti-war science fiction book.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Vonnegut's 1969 book about the firebombing of Dresden is a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: See 4
One's magic being the essence of Florence fun — and of Madrid, Blandings-style?

definitions.note: a style is a form of address, here for the Wodehouse pig

parts.note: one's is short for 'I am', IM
a peri is a fairy-like being of Persian myth
alma is Italian for soul, so the essence of someone in Florence
jest means fun or joking
y is the Spanish word for and

explanation.surface: Someone claims magic born of Florentine joy and Spanish flair, in the manner of a P G Wodehouse country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Blandings Castle is P G Wodehouse's comic setting, home of the prize pig called the Empress of Blandings; an empress is addressed by this title.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress, such as the Wodehouse prize sow, is formally addressed by this honorific title.

clue.text: She's shown off wiles in Slam Era

indicators.note: shown off suggests a display, the letters set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A star player has shown her cunning in tennis's Grand Slam period.
explanation.walkthrough: A Grand Slam is one of tennis's four major tournaments, which this player won many times.
explanation.definitionFit: The American tennis champion is a woman, so a feminine pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: See 18
Taciturn with sons and very this?

definitions.text: Taciturn with sons and very this?

indicators.note: this points to the answer itself as the instruction: swap the two letters of sons and very

parts.note: a reserved person is taciturn, saying little

explanation.surface: A quiet person with sons, and very much like this, asks a riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: S (sons) and V (very) change places in RESERVED; the answer word itself describes what has happened to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Swapping two letters' positions is turning them round, which is what the answer describes.

clue.text: When pub key's on top of roof?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone asks when the pub key is kept up on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: Asphalt was the usual surface on flat roofs before rolls of roofing felt.
explanation.definitionFit: A tar-based coating was traditionally laid on flat roofs as weatherproofing.

clue.text: Recall one European currency securing a second European guitar

definitions.note: a small four-stringed instrument of the guitar family

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run back the other way
one currency holds the other inside it

parts.note: the leu is Romania's currency
a second European currency, the lek of Albania

explanation.surface: Bring back one European currency that has secured a second, to buy a guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: Romania and Albania lie outside the eurozone, so their own currencies stand here for 'European currency'; 'Recall' turns the combined pair round before the final E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: This small Hawaiian instrument is a four-stringed member of the lute and guitar family.

clue.text: In the end, desperate lecturer needs daughter to stop a pain

indicators.note: the daughter acts as a stopper, plugged into the gap in the pain

parts.note: a stitch is a sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: A desperate academic finally needs his daughter to cure his sharp pain.
explanation.walkthrough: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt, made when all else has failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A final, desperate attempt is made at the last line of defence, at the end.

clue.text: Inferior port ol' jug dispensed on the rocks

indicators.note: the contents of the old jug are dispensed, poured out in a new order

parts.note: a drink on the rocks is served with ice

explanation.surface: Cheap port poured from an old jug over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers gives the phrase for poor port wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary term for bad wine of the fortified Portuguese type, as if it were wood sap.

clue.text: P*ss periodically taken out of Guardian's Ed?

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: A rude word is taken out of a Guardian editor's copy now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed is short for editor.
explanation.definitionFit: The asterisked vulgar word is slang for bodily waste liquid.

clue.text: Awkward metre gap having us in difficulties

indicators.note: awkward implies something clumsy, so the letters are put together differently

parts.note: us read as the plural of the letter U, so two Us

explanation.surface: An awkward gap in the metre leaves us struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is taken as U's, two letters U, which 'Awkward' mixes with METRE GAP. The phrase is an idiom for being in a fix, stuck like a treed animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being stuck in an awkward fix with no easy way down.

clue.text: Clever Clogs gets revenge, cooking kale and spinach?

indicators.note: cooking mixes the ingredients up into something new

parts.note: clever clogs, a show-off, is able, i.e. clever

explanation.surface: A know-all gets back at someone by serving up kale and spinach.
explanation.walkthrough: Clever Clogs is British slang for a smart-alec; here it gives ABLE, and 'cooking' stirs ABLE with GETS REVENGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are leafy plants of the cabbage and beet sort, eaten as dark leafy produce.

clue.text: Withdraw one from the local, maybe

parts.note: in local dialect one is 'un, as in 'a good 'un'
say means for example, maybe

explanation.surface: Someone backs out of buying a round at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The local is both a regional dialect and the neighbourhood pub; the surface wants the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back something spoken is to retract it.

clue.text: Close to border ring American number

indicators.note: the outer phrase borders, enclosing the inner pieces

parts.note: at hand means close by
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: Near the frontier a ring of American agents appears.
explanation.walkthrough: O and US go inside AT HAND, between its H and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand is a quantity, a large figure in counting.

clue.text: Unusual animal transported mineral to receiver

indicators.note: a receiver hears, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: sent means transported and ore is a mineral

explanation.surface: An odd creature carried minerals to a buyer of stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: SENT ORE said aloud gives the answer. A receiver looks like a fence for stolen goods but is a listener here.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical creature half man and half horse is certainly a strange beast.

clue.text: Distracted on Neverland holiday?

definitions.meaning: visiting Peter Pan's Neverland, home of Tinker Bell and her kind

explanation.surface: Someone is miles away, as if vacationing in Peter Pan's land.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means dreamily absent-minded; literally it suggests a trip among Tinker Bell's kind.

clue.text: Put odd present on a higher plane

indicators.note: odd suggests something out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Place a strange gift somewhere loftier.
explanation.walkthrough: Present looks like a gift, but means here, in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed aloft, at a lofty level, is overhead.

clue.text: Heroic tales endlessly put on reels

indicators.note: reels means spins round, so the letters are turned back to front
endlessly means without an end, so the word for put on loses its final letter

parts.note: added means put on, as of extra weight

explanation.surface: Old epics were endlessly wound onto film spools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ADDED to ADDE, and 'reels' turns that round, upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse collections of mythological poems and sagas are epic narratives.

clue.text: Direction possibly from minister Spooner's social workers observe in fold

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford dean, swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: bees are social insects and workers, and see means observe
pleated means in folds, like a skirt

explanation.surface: A clergyman's instruction about social workers watching sheep in a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: BEES SEE PLEATED, with opening sounds swapped, says the answer. A fold is also a sheep pen, the surface's picture for a minister's flock.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman leading a service may ask the congregation to sit.
